# Vendored PDF.js

This directory holds a **built and locally patched** copy of Mozilla's
[PDF.js](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js), committed to the repository rather
than installed at build time.

| | |
|---|---|
| upstream version | **2.10.0** (`pdfjsVersion` in `build/pdf.js`, `pdfjsBuild = c7a10e4`) |
| declared constraint | `pdfjs: ~2.10.x` in the top-level `bower.json` |
| build variant | `gulp generic-legacy`, regenerated by `make rebuild-pdfjs` |
| contents | `build/` (viewer + worker + sandbox), `web/`, `LICENSE` |

`bower` is only invoked by the manual `make rebuild-pdfjs` target. It is not part
of `make dist` and never runs in CI, so the committed copy is what ships.

## Applied patches

**This copy is not an unmodified 2.10.0 release.** Its version string still reads
`2.10.0`, so comparing that string against upstream will give the wrong answer
about what is fixed. Anything patched here must be listed below.

| advisory | severity | fixed upstream in | applied by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CVE-2024-4367](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wgrm-67xf-hhpq) — arbitrary JavaScript execution via a crafted `/FontMatrix` | HIGH | 4.2.67 | commit `3358e60`, [#351](https://github.com/owncloud/files_pdfviewer/pull/351) |

The fix rejects a `/FontMatrix` that is not exactly six numbers, falling back to
`FONT_IDENTITY_MATRIX`, so an attacker-controlled string cannot reach the glyph
command list. It is applied in both `build/pdf.js` and `build/pdf.worker.js` and
is marked in place with a `CVE-2024-4367:` comment.

## Security audit

Checked against the GitHub Advisory Database on 2026-09-09. Every published
`pdfjs-dist` advisory, and whether it applies to 2.10.0:

| advisory | affected range | applies here? |
|---|---|---|
| CVE-2024-4367 | `<= 4.1.392` | **yes** — backported, see above |
| CVE-2026-16633 | `>= 5.6.83, < 6.2.108` | no |
| CVE-2018-5158 | `>= 2.0.0, < 2.0.550` and `< 1.10.100` | no |

No known vulnerability is unpatched in this copy.

## Why there is a package.json and a .trivyignore

`package.json` exists so that vulnerability scanners and SBOM tooling can see
this library at all. Without it the vendored copy is invisible: it has no
manifest a scanner recognises, so `pdf.js` never appears in an inventory of what
this app ships — which is how a 2021-era PDF parser went unnoticed.

The cost of that visibility is one false positive: a scanner keyed on
`pdfjs-dist@2.10.0` reports CVE-2024-4367, which is backported here. The
repository-root `.trivyignore` accepts exactly that advisory and points back at
this file. Being listed with a documented exception is worth more than not being
listed at all.

## Updating

There is no automation. Bower has been unmaintained since 2017 and Dependabot has
never supported it, so nothing watches `pdfjs: ~2.10.x`.

To move to a newer upstream release:

1. Bump the constraint in the top-level `bower.json`.
2. Run `make rebuild-pdfjs` (needs `bower`, `npm` and `gulp`).
3. Re-check every entry in *Applied patches* against the new version. Drop the
   ones the new version already contains, and re-apply anything still needed.
4. Update the version, the build id and the audit date above, and prune
   `.trivyignore` accordingly.

Moving from 2.10.0 to a current 5.x is a breaking upgrade — the API, the viewer
layout and the build variants all changed — and it replaces bower with the
prebuilt `pdfjs-dist` npm package, which would also make Dependabot watch it.
That is tracked separately; it changes what `make dist` consumes, so it does not
belong in a patch release.
